Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024

contribution.value: SliceGPT is a post-training structured pruning method that applies an orthogonal transform (computational invariance) and slices entire rows and columns of weight matrices, reducing the embedding dimension while keeping competitive accuracy without recovery fine-tuning.

ev.quote: we present SliceGPT, a new post-training sparsification scheme which replaces each weight matrix with a smaller (dense) matrix, reducing the embedding dimension of the network
We experiment with two different calibration sets: the WikiText-2 training dataset
and the Alpaca training dataset (Taori et al., 2023)
We assess SliceGPT across five well-known zero-shot tasks: PIQA (Bisk et al., 2020)

data_size.value: Calibration set size 1024 sequences with sequence length 2048 (main experiments); ablations from 128 to 4096

ev.quote: Table 1: OPT and LLAMA-2 perplexity results on WikiText2. The calibration set size and sequence length are 1024 and 2048, respectively.
We evaluate all our experiments on OPT (Zhang et al., 2022), LLAMA-2 (Touvron et al., 2023) model families, and additionally evaluate Phi-2 (in our zero-shot task) experiments.
We begin by showcasing our findings using the WikiText-2 dataset. ... Table 1 shows the perplexity obtained by various slicing levels.

eval_metrics.value: Zero-shot accuracy (PIQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, ARC-e, ARC-c, average)

ev.quote: We assess SliceGPT across five well-known zero-shot tasks: PIQA ... WinoGrande ... HellaSwag ... ARC-e and ARCc

The token throughput of models sliced at 25% and 50% are compared to the dense model on 80GB H100 GPUs.

key_results.value: LLaMA-2 70B sliced 25% reaches WikiText-2 PPL 4.60 vs dense 3.32 (Δ 1.28); SparseGPT 2:4 reaches 4.98
Sliced models keep 99% (LLAMA-2 70B), 99% (OPT 66B) and 90% (Phi-2) of zero-shot accuracy at 25% slicing (90% Phi-2 with RFT)

ev.quote: SliceGPT can remove up to 25% of the model parameters (including embeddings) for LLAMA-2 70B, OPT 66B and Phi-2 models while maintaining 99%, 99% and 90% zero-shot task performance

ev.quote: With SliceGPT we compress large models using a single GPU in just a few hours and maintain competitive performance on generation and downstream tasks even without RFT.
The computation of Q is performed on a single H100 GPU with 80GB of memory, taking approximately 3.5 hours to complete for the LLAMA-2 70B model.
40GB A100s and 80GB H100s to provide datacenter-level benchmarks
Quadro RTX6000 GPUs with 24GB of memory as a representative example of consumer-level GPUs

value.baseline: FP16 dense LLaMA-2 70B (541 tokens/s on 2x H100)

strengths.value: Structured sliced models use dense kernels and run faster on standard hardware without custom sparse code.

ev.quote: Our sliced models run on fewer GPUs and run faster without any additional code optimization

strengths.value: Reduces inference compute on LLaMA-2 70B to 64% on RTX6000 and 66% on A100, cutting GPU count.

ev.quote: on 24GB consumer GPUs we reduce the total compute for inference on LLAMA-2 70B to 64% of that of the dense model; on 40GB A100 GPUs we reduce it to 66%

strengths.value: Single-shot method: no recovery fine-tuning needed to keep most accuracy at 25% slicing.

ev.section: ^(X) ^(W) Unstructured sparsity ^(X) ^(W) 2:4 Structured sparsity XQ ^(Q)^(⊤)^(W) Slicing (ours)
ev.quote: we compress large models using a single GPU in just a few hours and maintain competitive performance on generation and downstream tasks even without RFT

strengths.value: Beats SparseGPT 2:4 in WikiText-2 PPL on every LLaMA-2 size at 25% slicing.

ev.quote: Comparing SliceGPT with SparseGPT, we see that that SparseGPT 2:4 performs worse than SliceGPT with 25% slicing in all LLAMA-2 models.

weaknesses.value: Sliced LLaMA-2 models lose more accuracy than OPT models because LLaMA-2's eigenvalue spectrum is flatter.

ev.quote: SliceGPT exhibits superior performance when applied to OPT models compared to LLAMA-2 models which matches our intuition from the spectrum analysis

weaknesses.value: Smaller models (under 13B) gain less from slicing because they hold less spare embedding dimension.

ev.quote: Smaller but dense LMs perform better than LMs with 13B parameters or less pruned to similar sizes

weaknesses.value: Adds a small DxD residual-connection overhead per block that cannot be pre-computed.

ev.quote: these additional operations cannot be pre-computed and add a small (D × D) overhead to the model

weaknesses.value: Sliced models keep more parameters than SparseGPT 2:4 at matched compute, since slicing does not exploit unstructured zeros.

ev.quote: Our pruned models have more parameters than those pruned with SparseGPT but our method allows for larger batch sizes

limitations.value: Method is pruning-only and does not quantize weights or activations; quantization is left as complementary future work.

ev.quote: complementary methods including quantization (Xiao et al., 2023; Dettmers et al., 2022; Ashkboos et al., 2023; Dettmers et al., 2023; Frantar et al., 2022), and structural pruning ... could be used

limitations.value: Tested only on data-center class GPUs (RTX6000, A100, H100); no edge or mobile evaluation.

ev.quote: Quadro RTX6000 GPUs with 24GB of memory as a representative example of consumer-level GPUs; 40GB A100s and 80GB H100s to provide datacenter-level benchmarks

limitations.value: PCA needs double-precision eigendecomposition; FP32 PCA hurts perplexity, especially for larger models.

ev.quote: It shows that the accuracy of larger models could be affected by numerical errors during the PCA calculation phase.

limitations.value: No evaluation of safety, bias, jailbreak, or refusal after pruning.

future_work_stated.value: Combine SliceGPT with quantization and structural pruning to further reduce inference time and GPU count.

ev.quote: complementary methods including quantization ... and structural pruning (e.g. Ma et al., 2023b) could be used

future_work_stated.value: Explore alternative ways to compute the orthogonal matrix Q to improve accuracy.

ev.quote: Other methods of computing Q could improve the results.

future_work_stated.value: Combine slicing with sparsity to gain the benefits of both.

ev.quote: perhaps a combined method could obtain the best of both
providing energy and cost savings relative to deployment of the dense model
